evaluations.evidence: entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Specifies required data for the need rather than prescribing a concrete UI widget or technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific technical mechanism (invitation via URL) instead of stating the stakeholder need to invite estimators.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Unnecessarily prescribes a concrete UI widget (single multi-line text field).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need (visibility of items) without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user need (select an item) without unnecessary UI/technical prescription.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the need to add items; does not mandate a UI widget or technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the stakeholder need to edit items without prescribing how to implement editing.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: States the need to remove items; no UI/widget/technical solution is mandated.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the stakeholder need without prescribing a UI control or technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the desired outcome (use average) but does not mandate implementation specifics like algorithms or UI widgets.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Describes an automated behavior need; it does not prescribe a specific UI widget or low-level implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need to record the agreed estimate, without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user need to re-estimate; no solution details are mandated.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete technical mechanism (spreadsheet import) instead of stating the need to get stories into the system.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a particular method (copy/paste from spreadsheet) rather than the stakeholder need to quickly add stories.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: States the need to find past games without prescribing UI or technical details.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the stakeholder need (view transcript) without mandating a specific format or implementation.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific storage/transfer format (HTML) rather than simply stating the need to export transcripts.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete storage/format (CSV) instead of the general need to export for further processing.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to remove stored data without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Specifies required account information (data) rather than mandating a UI widget or technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: States the authentication need in common terms; does not prescribe a low-level implementation detail (e.g., specific auth protocol).

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Describes the stakeholder need without prescribing UI or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: States the need to remove personal data without mandating a particular technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a user-visible requirement (local timezone) without prescribing how conversions are implemented.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete technical communication mechanism (email) rather than expressing the general need to recover access.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Specifies user-configurable options (estimation scales) as part of the stakeholder need rather than low-level implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: States a capacity requirement (team size limit) without prescribing a technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: References a specific technical mechanism (joining via URL/page) rather than simply stating the need to join a game.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the user need to view the item without prescribing UI widgets or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: States the informational need without mandating a technical solution.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Describes a visibility need rather than prescribing how to implement that visibility.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the desired timing/visibility behavior without unnecessary implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: States the allowed interaction behavior; does not prescribe UI widgets or algorithms.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes an informational need without specifying UI or storage implementation.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need for attribution without prescribing a technical solution.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Describes a shared-timer feature need rather than prescribing an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Specifies desired automated behavior but does not force a particular technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Describes a navigation need without prescribing a specific UI control or low-level solution.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: States a consistency requirement (order) without imposing a technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Describes allowed user behavior rather than prescribing UI widgets or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific UI element (thumbnail photo and its placement) rather than the underlying need for personal identification.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete technology/standards (XHTML/CSS) as a solution choice instead of only stating accessibility/usability needs.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need for a glossary to ensure shared understanding without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a low-level implementation detail (database indexes) rather than stating the performance requirement.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Specifies particular browser versions (implementation/platform targets) rather than the general need for cross-browser compatibility.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a compliance goal (accessibility) rather than prescribing a specific widget or technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: States a non-functional user experience requirement (performance) without mandating implementation choices.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete technical mechanism/encoding (Unicode) rather than stating the higher-level need to support multiple languages.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Names a specific technical artifact (URLs) as the solution; the need could be expressed as understandable navigation without prescribing URL design.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Describes a user-facing quality need (friendly error pages) without mandating a specific technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: States a privacy requirement (non-identifiable storage) without prescribing a particular storage format or algorithm.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the stakeholder need for metrics without prescribing the metrics' storage format or implementation mechanism.
